a novel fractional order PID (FOPID) navigation guidance law is proposed by finite time stability (FTS) approach, whose stability conditions can be obtained analytically and can be utilized to determine the flight up time.
a novel fractional order guidance law is proposed to improve the performance of intercepting incoming targets.
a novel fractional order PID guidance law is proposed to achieve robust performance against maneuvering targets.

the design of a novel fractional order PID guidance law for missile interceptors.
the development of the novel fractional order PID guidance law, which has better performance than the conventional proportional navigation and proportional integral navigation guidance laws.
the design of a robust navigation guidance law for the intercepting maneuvering targets.

the proposed guidance laws can achieve better performance when compared with the proportional navigation guidance law.

the proposed fractional order PID guidance law is a robust and effective guidance law for intercepting incoming maneuvering targets, and it is also a good alternative to the conventional PID guidance law.
the proposed guidance method is more effective and robust in intercepting incoming targets with a wide range of maneuvering capabilities.

a new guidance law with finite time stability analysis is developed for the 6 degrees-of freedom missile guidance problem.
the proposed guidance laws can achieve the intercepting incoming target robustly and efficiently.

the proposed navigation guidance law can achieve better performance than the traditional guidance laws, which can be used to guide the interceptor to intercept incoming targets with high accuracy and robustness.
